indexDefinitions: U.S. Large Cap Equities (MSCI USA (USD) Total Return Index). The MSCI USA Index is designed to measure the performance of the large and mid cap segments of the US market. The index covers approximately 85% of the free float-adjusted market capitalization in the US.

U.S. Value (MSCI USA Value (USD) Total Return Index). The MSCI USA Value Index captures large and mid cap US securities exhibiting overall value style characteristics. The value investment style characteristics for index construction are defined using three variables: book value to price, 12-month forward earnings to price and dividend yield.

U.S. Growth (MSCI USA Growth (USD) Total Return Index). The MSCI USA Growth Index captures large and mid cap securities exhibiting overall growth style characteristics in the US. The growth investment style characteristics for index construction are defined using five variables: long-term forward EPS growth rate, short-term forward EPS growth rate, current internal growth rate and long-term historical EPS growth trend and long-term historical sales per share growth trend.

U.S. Momentum (MSCI USA Momentum (USD) Total Return Index). The MSCI USA Momentum Index is based on MSCI USA Index, its parent index, which captures large and mid cap stocks of the US market. It is designed to reflect the performance of an equity momentum strategy by emphasizing stocks with high price momentum, while maintaining reasonably high trading liquidity, investment capacity and moderate index turnover.

U.S. Quality (MSCI USA Quality (USD) Total Return Index). The MSCI USA Quality Index is based on the MSCI USA Index, its parent index, which includes large and mid cap stocks in the US equity market. The index aims to capture the performance of quality growth stocks by identifying stocks with high quality scores based on three main fundamental variables: high return on equity (ROE), stable year-over-year earnings growth and low financial leverage.

U.S. Low Volatility (MSCI USA Minimum Volatility (USD) Total Return Index). The MSCI USA Minimum Volatility (USD) Index aims to reflect the performance characteristics of a minimum variance strategy applied to the large and mid cap USA equity universe. The index is calculated by optimizing the MSCI USA Index, its parent index, in USD for the lowest absolute risk (within a given set of constraints).

U.S. Small Cap Equities (Russell 2000 Total Return Index). The Russell 2000® Index measures the performance of the small-cap segment of the US equity universe. The Russell 2000 Index is a subset of the Russell 3000® Index which is designed to represent approximately 98% of the investable US equity market. It includes approximately 2,000 of the smallest securities based on a combination of their market cap and current index membership. The Russell 2000 is constructed to provide a comprehensive and unbiased small-cap barometer and is completely reconstituted annually to ensure larger stocks do not distort the performance and characteristics of the true small-cap opportunity set.

U.S Small Cap Value (Russell 2000 Value Total Return Index). Russell 2000 Value Index measures the performance of those Russell 2000 companies with lower price-to-book ratios and lower forecasted growth values.

International Equities (MSCI EAFE Net Return Index USD). The MSCI EAFE Index is an equity index which captures large and mid cap representation across Developed Markets countries around the world, excluding the US and Canada. The index covers approximately 85% of the free float-adjusted market capitalization in each country.

International Value (MSCI EAFE Value Net Return Index USD). The MSCI EAFE Value Index captures large and mid cap securities exhibiting overall value style characteristics across Developed Markets countries* around the world, excluding the US and Canada. The value investment style characteristics for index construction are defined using three variables: book value to price, 12-month forward earnings to price and dividend yield. The index targets 50% coverage of the free float-adjusted market capitalization of the MSCI EAFE Index.

Global Equities (MSCI ACWI Net Return Index USD). The MSCI ACWI captures large and mid cap representation across Developed Markets (DM) and Emerging Markets (EM) countries. The index covers approximately 85% of the global investable equity opportunity set.

Emerging Market Equities (MSCI Emerging Markets Net Return Index USD). The MSCI Emerging Markets Index captures large and mid cap representation across Emerging Markets (EM) countries. The index covers approximately 85% of the free float-adjusted market capitalization in each country.

Emerging Markets Value (MSCI Emerging Markets Value Net Return Index USD). The MSCI Emerging Markets Value Index captures large and mid cap securities exhibiting overall value characteristics across Emerging Markets (EM) countries. The value investment style characteristics for index construction are defined using three variables: book value to price, 12-month forward earnings to price and dividend yield. The index targets 50% coverage of the free float-adjusted market capitalization of the MSCI EM Index.

U.S. Treasury Ladder (ReSolve U.S. Treasury Ladder Index). An internal index that equally weights the returns of four U.S. Treasury futures contracts (2-Year, 5-Year, 10-Year, and Long Bond), plus a 100% allocation to the Bloomberg US Treasury Bills 1-3 Month TR Index (LD12TRUU) as collateral return. Futures returns are constructed by ReSolve Asset Management Inc. using a front-month rolling methodology, whereby each contract is rolled prior to expiry.

U.S. Core Fixed Income (Bloomberg US Agg Total Return Value Unhedged USD). The Bloomberg USAgg Index is a broad-based flagship benchmark that measures the investment grade, US dollar-denominated, fixed-rate taxable bond market. The index includes Treasuries, government-related and corporate securities, MBS (agency fixed-rate pass-throughs), ABS and CMBS (agency and non-agency).

U.S. Treasuries (Bloomberg US Treasury Total Return Index). The Bloomberg US Treasury Index measures US dollar-denominated, fixed-rate, nominal debt issued by the US Treasury. Treasury bills are excluded by the maturity constraint but are part of a separate Short Treasury Index. STRIPS are excluded from the index because their inclusion would result in double-counting.

Short-Term U.S. Treasuries (Bloomberg US Treasury 1-5 Year Total Return Index). The Bloomberg US Treasury Index measures US dollar-denominated, fixed-rate, nominal debt issued by the US Treasury. Treasury bills are excluded by the maturity constraint, but are part of a separate Short Treasury Index.

Intermediate-term U.S. Treasuries (Bloomberg US Intermediate Treasury TR Index Value Unhedged USD). The Bloomberg US Treasury: Intermediate Index measures US dollar-denominated, fixed-rate, nominal debt issued by the US Treasury with maturities of 1 to 9.9999 years to maturity.

Long-Term U.S. Treasuries (Bloomberg US Long Treasury Total Return Index Value Unhedged USD). The Bloomberg US Treasury: Long Index measures US dollar-denominated, fixed-rate, nominal debt issued by the US Treasury with 10 years or more to maturity.

U.S. Corporate Fixed Income (Bloomberg US Corporate Index). The Bloomberg US Corporate Index measures the investment grade, fixed-rate, taxable corporate bond market. It includes USD-denominated securities publicly issued by US and non-US industrial, utility, and financial issuers.

Short-Term Investment Grade Fixed Income (Bloomberg US Credit 1-5 years Total Return Index Value Unhedged USD). The Bloomberg US Corporate Bond 1-5 Year Index measures the investment grade, fixed-rate, taxable corporate bond market with 1-5 year maturities.

Intermediate-Term Investment Grade Fixed Income (Bloomberg US Credit Corp 5-10Y Total Return Index Value Unhedged USD). The Bloomberg US Corporate Bond 1-5 Year Index measures the investment grade, fixed-rate, taxable corporate bond market with 5-10 year maturities.

Long-Term Investment Grade Fixed Income (Bloomberg U.S. 10+ Year Corporate Bond Total Return Index Unhedged USD). The Index measures the performance of the long-dated, investment grade U.S. corporate bond market. Only bonds that have a maturity of more than ten years are included. Securities must be fixed rate, U.S. dollar denominated, taxable and rated investment grade as defined by the Index methodology. Inclusion is based on the currency of the issue, not the domicile of the issuer.

High Yield Fixed Income (Bloomberg US Corporate High Yield Total Return Index Value Unhedged USD). The Bloomberg US Corporate High Yield Bond Index measures the USD-denominated, high yield, fixed-rate corporate bond market. Securities are classified as high yield if the middle rating of Moody's, Fitch and S&P is Ba1/BB+/BB+ or below. Bonds from issuers with an emerging markets country of risk, based on Bloomberg EM country definition, are excluded.

Mortgage Backed Securities (Bloomberg US MBS Index Total Return Value Unhedged USD). The Bloomberg US Mortgage Backed Securities (MBS) Index tracks fixed-rate agency mortgage backed pass-through securities guaranteed by Ginnie Mae (GNMA), Fannie Mae (FNMA), and Freddie Mac (FHLMC). The index is constructed by grouping individual TBA-deliverable MBS pools into aggregates or generics based on program, coupon and vintage.

International Treasuries (Bloomberg Global Treasury x US Capped Total Return Index Value Unhedged USD). The Bloomberg Global Treasury ex US Index is a subset of the flagship Global Treasury Index that does not have any exposure to US debt. This multi-currency benchmark includes investment grade, fixed-rate bonds issued by governments in their native currencies.

Global Core Fixed Income (Bloomberg Global-Aggregate Total Return Index Value Unhedged USD). The Bloomberg GlobalAgg Index is a flagship measure of global investment grade debt from a multitude local currency markets. This multi-currency benchmark includes treasury, government-related, corporate and securitized fixed-rate bonds from both developed and emerging markets issuers.

Emerging Market Bonds (Local) (J.P. Morgan Government Bond Index-Emerging Markets Global Core Net Return Index). The GBI-EM Global Diversified Core (GBI-EM Global Core) is designed to track the performance of bonds issued by emerging market governments and denominated in the local currency of the issuer. The GBI-EM Core is designed to be
investible and is based on the well-established methodology and composition of the flagship GBI-EM Global Diversified index. The main enhancement of the GBI-EM Global Core is that it applies a maximum country weight of 10% (cap) and minimum country weight of 1% to 3% (floor) based on the country’s eligible debt outstanding. The index includes only
those countries that are accessible by most of the international investor base and selects bonds from each of the emerging market countries set forth below that are fixed-rate, domestic currency government bonds with greater than 13 months to maturity.

Emerging Market Bonds (USD) (J.P. Morgan Emerging Markets Bond Index Global Core Net Return Index). The J.P. Morgan Emerging Markets Bond Index Global Core (EMBIG CORE) tracks liquid, US dollar emerging market fixed and floating-rate debt instruments issued by sovereign and quasi sovereign entities . The EMBIG CORE is based on the long established flagship JPMorgan EMBI Global and follows its methodology closely, while offering a more liquid subset of the index by removing the instruments with smaller face amounts outstanding and the instruments that are closer to maturity. The diversification methodology limits the weights of the larger index countries by only including a specified portion of those countries' eligible current face amounts of debt outstanding, thus providing a more even distribution of weights across the countries in the index. The Returns and Statistics are available from Dec 1997.

Real Estate (Dow Jones U.S. Select REIT Total Return Index). The Dow Jones U.S. Select REIT Index tracks the performance of publicly traded REITs and REIT-like securities and is designed to serve as a proxy for direct real estate investment, in part by excluding companies whose performance may be driven by factors other than the value of real estate. The index is a subset of the Dow Jones U.S. Select Real Estate Securities Index (RESI), which represents equity real estate investment trusts (REITs) and real estate operating companies (REOCs) traded in the U.S.

Commodities (S&P GSCI Index Spot Index). The S&P GSCI® is widely recognized as a leading measure of general price movements and inflation in the world economy. It provides investors with a reliable and publicly available benchmark for investment performance in the commodity markets.
Gold (XAU Currency). Gold spot price quoted in USD per ounce.
Digital Assets (S&P Bitcoin Index). The S&P Bitcoin Index is designed to track the performance of the digital asset Bitcoin.

Short-Term TIPS (Bloomberg US Treasury TIPS 0-5 Years Total Return Index Unhedged USD). The Bloomberg US Treasury Inflation-Linked Bond Index (Series-L) measures the performance of the US Treasury Inflation Protected Securities (TIPS) market with 0-5 year maturities. Federal Reserve holdings of US TIPS are not index eligible and are excluded from the face amount outstanding of each bond in the index.

Intermediate-Term TIPS (Bloomberg US Treasury Inflation Notes TR Index Value Unhedged USD). The Bloomberg US Treasury Inflation-Linked Bond Index (Series-L) measures the performance of the US Treasury Inflation Protected Securities (TIPS) market. Federal Reserve holdings of US TIPS are not index eligible and are excluded from the face amount outstanding of each bond in the index.

Long Volatility (CBOE Eurekahedge Long Volatility Hedge Fund Index). The CBOE Eurekahedge Long Volatility Index is an equally weighted index of 15 constituent funds. The index is designed to provide a broad measure of the performance of underlying hedge fund managers who take a net long view on implied volatility with a goal of positive absolute return. The CBOE Eurekahedge Long Volatility Index is a collaborative index between Eurekahedge and the Chicago Board Options Exchange.

Tail Risk Hedges (CBOE Eurekahedge Tail Risk Hedge Fund Index). The CBOE Eurekahedge Tail Risk Index is an equally weighted index of the constituent funds. The index is designed to provide a broad measure of the performance of underlying hedge fund managers that specifically seek to achieve capital appreciation during periods of extreme market stress. The CBOE Eurekahedge Tail Risk Index is a collaborative index between Eurekahedge and the Chicago Board Options Exchange.

Equity Long/Short (PivotalPath Equity Diversified: Global Long/Short Index). The PivotalPath Equity Diversified: Global Long/Short Hedge Fund Index is an equal weighted index which comprises funds that primarily invest long and short in equities across all geographies. The Index tracks the monthly performance, net of fees in USD, of its constituents a minimum fund track record of 18 months and a minimum fund AUM of $50mm. The constituents are fixed at the end each calendar year for the following calendar year.

Hedge Funds (PivotalPath Composite EW Index). The PivotalPath Composite Hedge Fund Index is a global, equal-weighted index tracking qualified institutional quality funds covered by firm research. The constituent funds report monthly performance, net of all fees, in USD. The Index is representative of hedge fund performance across all strategies and geographies with a minimum fund track record of 18 months and a minimum fund AUM of $50mm. The constituents are fixed at the end each calendar year for the following calendar year.

Equity Market Neutral (EurekaHedge Equity Market Neutral Hedge Fund Index). The Eurekahedge Equity Market Neutral Hedge Fund Index (Bloomberg Ticker - EHFI751) is an equally weighted index of 28 constituent funds. The index is designed to provide a broad measure of the performance of underlying hedge fund managers. The index is base weighted at 100 at Dec 1999, does not contain duplicate funds and is denominated in local currencies.

Event Driven (PivotalPath Event Driven Index). The PivotalPath Event Driven Hedge Fund Index is an asset weighted index of strategies seeking to exploit pricing inefficiencies that may occur before or after a corporate event. The index is asset weighted by three sub-strategies (equity special situations, merger arbitrage, & multi-event) and tracks the monthly performance, net of fees in USD, of funds with a minimum fund track record of 18 months and a minimum fund AUM of $50mm. The constituents are fixed at the end each calendar year for the following calendar year.

Merger Arbitrage (PivotalPath Event Driven : Merger Arbitrage Index). The PivotalPath Event Driven: Merger Arbitrage Hedge Fund Index is an equal weighted index which comprises funds that typically purchase shares in one company and short sell the assets in another. The strategy is generally used in the expectation of a pending announcement of a company takeover, where the fund will take a long position in the target firm and a short position in the acquiring firm. The Index tracks the monthly performance, net of fees in USD, of its constituents with a minimum fund track record of 18 months and a minimum fund AUM of $50mm. The constituents are fixed at the end each calendar year for the following calendar year

Relative Value (PivotalPath Credit: Relative Value Index). The PivotalPath Credit: Relative Value Hedge Fund Index is an equal weighted index which comprises funds that aim to capture price differences in opportunities across the credit spectrum. The Index tracks the monthly performance, net of fees in USD, of its constituents with a minimum fund track record of 18 months and a minimum fund AUM of $50mm. The constituents are fixed at the end each calendar year for the following calendar year.

Managed Futures CTA (PivotalPath Managed Futures Index). The PivotalPath Managed Futures Hedge Fund Index is an equal weighted index of funds that typically forecast market trends and determine whether to invest long or short in futures contracts across metals, grains, equity indices and soft commodities, as well as foreign currency and U.S. government bond futures. The Index tracks the monthly performance, net of fees in USD, of its constituents and is representative of funds with a minimum fund track record of 18 months and a minimum fund AUM of $50mm. The constituents are fixed at the end each calendar year for the following calendar year.

Futures Yield (Carry) (ReSolve Futures Yield Liquid Universe Index). ReSolve Futures Yield Liquid Universe Index seeks to harness carry returns from a diversified set of global futures markets spanning equity indices, government bonds, currencies, and commodities. The strategy maximizes long positions in assets with positive carry and short exposure to markets with negative carry, while managing overall portfolio risk through an advanced optimization method designed to maximize portfolio diversity and minimize unproductive trading. The index is calculated net of modeled transaction costs and a 0.95% annual management fee. The index inception date is 5/30/2024; all data prior to that date is backtested.

Managed Futures Trend (SG Trend Index). The SG Trend Index is equal-weighted and reconstituted annually. The index calculates the net daily rate of return for a pool of trend following based hedge fund managers.

Risk Parity (10%) (S&P Risk Parity Index - 10% Volatility Target). The S&P Risk Parity Index - 10% Target Volatility seeks to measure the performance of a multi-asset risk parity strategy that allocates risk equally among equity, fixed income, and commodities futures contracts, while targeting a volatility level of 10%.

Risk Parity (12%) (S&P Risk Parity Index - 12% Target Volatility). The S&P Risk Parity Index - 12% Target Volatility seeks to measure the performance of a multi-asset risk parity strategy that allocates risk equally among equity, fixed income, and commodities futures contracts, while targeting a volatility level of 12%.

Risk Parity (15%) (S&P Risk Parity Index - 15% Volatility Target). The S&P Risk Parity Index - 15% Target Volatility seeks to measure the performance of a multi-asset risk parity strategy that allocates risk equally among equity, fixed income, and commodities futures contracts, while targeting a volatility level of 15%.

Global Macro (PivotalPath Global Macro Index). The PivotalPath Global Macro Hedge Fund Index is an asset weighted index of strategies seeking to profit from the broad market swings caused by political or economic events. These funds generally participate in major markets including equities, bonds, currencies, and commodities, and use financial instruments to maintain long and short positions based on their research of the global market environment. The Index is asset weighted by five sub-strategies (commodities, discretionary, multi-manager, quantitative, & risk premia) and tracks the monthly performance, net of fees in USD, of funds with a minimum fund track record of 18 months and a minimum fund AUM of $50mm. The constituents are fixed at the end each calendar year for the following calendar year.

Global Macro (Commodities) (PivotalPath Global Macro: Commodities Index). The PivotalPath Global Macro: Commodities Hedge Fund Index is an equal weighted index which comprises funds that have a commodity-focused approach to global macro investing. The Index tracks the monthly performance, net of fees in USD, of its constituents with a minimum fund track record of 18 months and a minimum fund AUM of $50mm. The constituents are fixed at the end each calendar year for the following calendar year.

Systematic Global Macro (PivotalPath Global Macro: Quantitative Index). The PivotalPath Global Macro: Quantitative Hedge Fund Index is an equal weighted index which comprises funds that typically use a quantitative approach to systematically invest across multiple geographies and asset classes. The Index tracks the monthly performance, net of fees in USD, of its constituents with a minimum fund track record of 18 months and a minimum fund AUM of $50mm. The constituents are fixed at the end each calendar year for the following calendar year.

Global Macro (Risk Premia) (PivotalPath Global Macro: Risk Premia Index). The PivotalPath Global Macro: Risk Premia Hedge Fund Index is an equal weighted index which comprises funds that target absolute returns through long and short positions across various factors and asset classes in the global market landscape. The Index tracks the monthly performance, net of fees in USD, of its constituents with a minimum fund track record of 18 months and a minimum fund AUM of $50mm. The constituents are fixed at the end each calendar year for the following calendar year.

Stock / Bond Momentum (Newfound/ReSolve Robust Equity Momentum TR Index). The Newfound / ReSolve Robust Equity Momentum Index attempts to provide dynamic exposure to broad U.S., international, and emerging equities while simultaneously seeking to avoid significant and prolonged drawdowns by tactically allocating to short- or intermediate-term U.S. Treasuries. Exposures to underlying indices are expressed through U.S. listed Exchange Traded Funds (”ETFs”). The Index rebalances weekly into the equity region exhibiting the strongest momentum (subject to constraints on maximum weights). A trend filter is applied, allocating into U.S. Treasuries when equities exhibit negative trends. The Index employs an ensemble approach where a large number of simple momentum and trend strategies ”vote” on which of the 5 possible ETFs should be held by the Index. The weight of each ETF in the portfolio at each rebalance is in proportion to the percentage of votes it receives.

Risk-Weighted Gold/Bitcoin (Kaiko Bytree BOLD1 Inverse Volatility Index). The Kaiko Bytetree BOLD1 Inverse Volatility Index comprises bitcoin and gold, and rebalances monthly according to the inverse historic volatility (360-day) of each asset.

Cash (Bloomberg US Treasury Bill Total Return Index Unhedged USD). The Bloomberg US Treasury Bill Index tracks the market for treasury bills issued by the US government. US Treasury bills are issued in fixed maturity terms of 4, 13, 26 and 52 weeks. The US Treasury Bill Index is a component of the US Short Treasury Index along with US Treasury notes and bonds that have fallen below one year to maturity. Bloomberg publishes sub-indices based on the following maturities: 1-3 months, 3-6 months, 6-9 months and 9-12 months, to measure the performance of treasury bills of specific tenors. The index was launched in May 1997, with index history backfilled to December 1, 1991.

The PivotalPath index/indices used in this information is/are produced by the hedge fund research and investment consultancy firm, PivotalPath Inc. The information is representative of the overall composition of the hedge fund universe, as well as specific sub-strategies, including but not limited to the PivotalPath Hedge Fund Composite Index; the PivotalPath Credit Index (and associated sub-indices); the PivotalPath Equity Diversified Index (and associated subindices); the PivotalPath Equity Sector Index (and associated sub-indices); the PivotalPath Event Driven Index (and associated sub-indices); the PivotalPath Global Macro Index (and associated sub-indices); the PivotalPath Managed Futures Index; the PivotalPath Multi-Strategy Index; PivotalPath Equity Quant Index; and the PivotalPath Volatility Index.

Statistics Definitions
Volatility: Statistical measure of price fluctuations representing the degree of variation in an investment's returns over time, calculated as standard deviation of monthly returns and annualized.

Skewness: Measure of asymmetry in return distribution, indicating whether returns are concentrated on one side of the mean, with positive values suggesting more extreme positive returns and negative values indicating more extreme negative returns.
Kurtosis: Metric describing the shape of a return distribution's tail relative to a normal distribution, measuring the likelihood of extreme outcomes beyond standard deviations.

Sharpe Ratio: Risk-adjusted performance metric calculated by dividing excess returns (portfolio return minus risk-free rate, measured by the Bloomberg US Treasury Bill Total Return index Unhedged USD Index) by portfolio volatility, indicating return per unit of risk.

Probabilistic Sharpe Ratio: Adjusted Sharpe ratio (Bailey and DePrado, 2008) that accounts for estimation uncertainty by considering the probability that the true Sharpe ratio is statistically significant. This metric can be interpreted as the probability that the Sharpe Ratio is greater than a benchmark Sharpe Ratio.
Sortino Ratio: Performance measure similar to Sharpe ratio but using downside deviation instead of total volatility, focusing exclusively on harmful price variations.

Upside Capture: Measures a portfolio's performance relative to a benchmark during periods when the benchmark rose. Calculated as the portfolio's compound annualized return over the months in which the benchmark (the Core portfolio) posted a positive return, divided by the benchmark's compound annualized return over those same months. A value above 100% indicates the portfolio captured more than the benchmark's gains in up markets, while a value below 100% indicates it captured less. The benchmark's capture against itself is 100% by definition.

Downside Capture: Measures a portfolio's performance relative to a benchmark during periods when the benchmark declined. Calculated as the portfolio's compound annualized return over the months in which the benchmark (the Core portfolio) posted a negative return, divided by the benchmark's compound annualized return over those same months. A value below 100% indicates the portfolio experienced less than the benchmark's losses in down markets, while a value above 100% indicates it experienced more. A negative value indicates the portfolio gained, on average, during the benchmark's down months. The benchmark's capture against itself is 100% by definition.
Calmar Ratio: Performance metric calculated by dividing average annual return by maximum drawdown, evaluating investment performance relative to its worst historical decline.
Tail Ratio: Comparative measurement of portfolio's extreme positive (95th percentile) and negative (fifth percentile) returns, helping assess asymmetric risk distribution.
Diversification Ratio: Metric quantifying portfolio risk reduction through asset allocation, comparing portfolio volatility to weighted individual asset volatilities.
Max Drawdown: Largest percentage drop from peak to trough in investment value before a new peak is achieved, indicating maximum potential loss.
Average Drawdown: Mean percentage decline experienced by an investment across multiple drawdown periods.
1-Year 95% VaR (Value at Risk): Maximum potential loss with 95% confidence over a one-year period, representing a specific percentile of worst-case scenarios.
1-Year 95% CVaR (Conditional Value at Risk): Expected loss beyond the 95% VaR threshold, providing a more conservative risk estimate by calculating the average of losses exceeding the VaR level.

Merger Arbitrage (AB) (AlphaBeta Merger Arbitrage Index). The AlphaBeta Merger Arbitrage Index is a long-short, event-driven index that uses a pricing model to estimate expected returns on M&A deals involving U.S.-listed public companies, targeting an average annual performance of the risk-free rate plus 4%. It includes only stock and stock-and-cash deals that meet its criteria for expected return and probability of completion. Constituent weights are dynamically adjusted based on deal size, market liquidity, and expected downside risk to keep the index both representative of significant merger activity and investable. The index inception date is 12/17/2024; all data prior to that date is backtested.
